subject: Acme Health — SKU licensing tiers, private offer structure & partner margin reconciliation
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace packaging question — seat + consumption SKUs and reseller passback

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We pulled together a short RFP fragment that describes our expected usage profile for the next 12 months (attached). Two questions up front as we evaluate Redwood for an AWS private offer:

1) We plan to sell a bundled solution to our clinics: a per-seat license (monthly) plus a metered consumption SKU for inference tokens. Can Redwood list both SKUs in a single private offer without requiring stacking/list-price escalation that would hurt the partner margin?

2) What does a typical reseller passback look like on your side when selling via a partner (reseller)? Our procurement team is asking for an expected % so they can include it in their T&Cs.

We also want an example of the private offer price breakdown (list price vs net to reseller vs Redwood list) to show our procurement and accounting teams.

Attached: Acme_RFP_Sept2026.pdf

Best,
Maria
Maria Lopez
Head of Procurement
Acme Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging question — seat + consumption SKUs and reseller passback

Hi Maria — thanks for the note and the RFP. High level answers below; I included Ben and Vivek for margin/ops validation.

Short answers:
- Yes — AWS/GCP/Azure private offers can list multiple SKUs in one offer. We recommend keeping seat and consumption separate SKUs in the PO so you can track usage and apply different billing cadence.
- Typical reseller passback on similar deals ranges 10–18% depending on commit length and co-sell obligations.

Proposal (starter):
- Seat SKU: monthly per-seat list $125 / seat.
- Consumption SKU: metered token price $0.0009 / token (first 10M tokens discount ladder).
- Reseller passback: 15% of Redwood list for the first 12 months, with an early-adopter credit applied as a separate line item in month 1.

Why this structure?
- Separating SKUs avoids list-price stacking that complicates invoicing and partner splits.
- Explicit early-adopter credit preserves partner economics while keeping net list tidy for marketplace reporting.

I've attached a quick price matrix with the above starter numbers for Acme to review. Ben — can you confirm this is feasible from a partner-margin perspective and flag any tax/listing constraints we should surface to Maria? Vivek — please check if this plays with our AWS private offer BOM (buckets/price dimensions).

Attachments: PO_price_matrix_v1.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a call later this week with Maria and AWS marketplace if helpful.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Growth, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging question — seat + consumption SKUs and reseller passback

Thanks Priya — quick margin sanity check after running the attached model. Maria — cc'ing to be transparent.

Key observations:
- If we set a 15% reseller passback on Redwood list and keep the seat @ $125 and token @ $0.0009, the reseller net margin falls to ~8% after marketplace fees (AWS fee ~5%), payment processing, and expected distributor handling. That is below the typical reseller target for your channel partners (12–15%).

Options to preserve partner economics:
1) Reduce reseller passback to 12% and provide a one-time $50k early-adopter credit to Acme (applied as an upfront reimbursement via the private-offer line item).
2) Keep 15% passback but raise seat list to $135 (small list uplift) and widen the token price ladder to give partners higher margin on overage buckets.

Operational notes:
- Any one-time credits should be a separate non-billable line in the private offer so marketplace reconciliation stays clean.
- Taxes and local VAT for clinics in EU states will change the effective net; if Acme has EU clinics we need to model that separately.

Attachment: margin_model_acme.csv (contains assumption set and per-region net calculations)

My recommendation: Option 1 (12% passback + $50k credit) keeps list prices customer-friendly and preserves partner economics without re-listing SKUs. Priya — if Acme signs a 12-month commit with a 10% uplift year 2, we can revisit margin cadence.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Partner Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
